tier_reason: The README table (Mistral-7B-Instruct-v0.2 FP16, 4k context, RTX 4090 + EPYC 7702P) gives first-party tok/s for huggingface transformers 25.9/25.7, llama.cpp 61.0/58.8, calm 66.0/65.7 and yalm 63.8/58.7, matching the record. No harness script for the cross-engine table, no baseline versions and no toolchain versions are given, so C.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Makefile: host C++ -O3 -ffast-math -std=c++20 -fopenmp -mf16c -mavx2 -mfma; nvcc -O2 -lineinfo with default -gencode sm_80 and sm_90 (or -arch=$(CUARCH)). The compiler and CUDA versions and the CUARCH used for the RTX 4090 run are not stated.
corrections.caveats: Only the margin over Hugging Face transformers is large (about 2.5x and 2.3x); against llama.cpp it is +4.6% at ~120 tokens and 58.7 vs 58.8 tok/s (a tie, marginally slower) at ~4800 tokens, and the README shows calm ahead of yalm at both lengths. Versions and settings of transformers and llama.cpp are not stated, the repo has no script that reproduces the cross-engine table (./build/test only benchmarks yalm's own kernels and memory bandwidth), and the CUDA and compiler versions are not given. The author calls it an educational exercise not meant for production; single GPU only, model must fit in VRAM, a few models tested. No LICENSE file in the repo root, so the code is reference only. The author's blog post 'Fast LLM Inference From Scratch' (andrewkchan.dev, also an HN thread) was not opened because personal blogs are egress-blocked; a WebSearch snippet only repeated the README table.

notes: Numbers verified verbatim on the README; metadata confirmed on github.com (no license shown, 602 stars, 64 forks, not a fork or archived, last commit 2025-08-26, so stale against 2026-09-26). No shortcoming beyond the thin margin over llama.cpp and the missing license.
